title: Why Your Sink Drains Slowly (And What's Trapped Inside)
description: Most sink blockages happen right inside the P-trap—the curved pipe section located directly beneath your sink basin. In kitchens, melted fats, cooking oils, and fine food particles collect at the bottom of this trap, cooling and solidifying into a dense barrier over time. In bathrooms, soap residue binds with hair to restrict water flow. Rinsing oils down the drain with cold water speeds up this buildup, narrowing the pipe's internal diameter. To protect your drainage, scrape plates into the trash, never pour liquid fat down the drain, and flush sinks periodically with hot water. For persistent slow drains, a professional inspection prevents pipe damage.
